sections.label: Mind
sections.text:
Loquacity and delirium from eating acid
fruits. Depression of spirits.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
Vertigo, with tendency to fall forward.
Headache, dull pressure, worse morning, with heated
face and bitter taste; alternating ivith diarrhoea. Roll’
ing of head from side to side, with moaning and vomit-
ing and eyelids half closed. Child perspires on head
during sleep.

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Grinding the teeth at night; intense desire
to press the gums together. [Fhytol.] Difficult den- w
tition. Tongue broad, large, moist. Foul, putrid taste.
Burning sensation of tongue.

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Hot, sour belching; nausea and vomit-
ing. Thirst for large quantities of cold water. [Bry.]
Vomiting of hot, frothy mucus. Heartburn ; gagging
or empty retching. Vomiting of milk.

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Distended ; heat and emptiness. Sensa-
tion of weakness or sinking. Can lie comfortably only
on stomach. Liver region painful, better rubbing part.
Rumbling and shifting of flatus in ascending colon.

sections.label: Rectum
sections.text:
Cholera infantum and morbus. Diar-
rhoea of long standing; early in morning; during teeth’
ing, with hoi, glowing cheeks while being bathed or
washed; in hot weather after acid fruits. Morning,
painless diarrhoea when not due to venous stasis or intes-
tinal ulceration. Green, watery, fetid, profuse, gushing.
Prolapse of rectum before or with stool. Constipation;
clay-colored, hard, dry, difficult. Constipation alternating
with diarrhoea [Ant. crud.] Internal and external
piles.

sections.label: Female
sections.text:
Pain in uterus and right ovary, with shift-
ing gases along ascending colon. Suppressed menses,

with pelvic tenesmus. Prolapsed uteri, especially after
parturition. Haemorrhoids, with prolapsus ani during
pregnancy. Prolapsus from overlifting or straining;
during pregnancy. Frequent urination at night.

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Pain between shoulders, under right
scapula, in loins and lumbar region. Pain in right in-
guinal region ; shoots down inner thigh to knee. Paraly-
tic weakness on left side.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Chill at 7 a. m., with pain in hypochondria,
and knees, ankles, wrists. Great loquacity during fever.
Profuse sweat.

sections.label: Modalities
sections.text:
Worse, in early morning, in hot
weather, during dentition.

sections.label: Relationship
sections.text:
Compare: Aloe; Chelid.; Mere.:
Nux; Sulph.

Griping pain, with great rumbling,
nausea, and liquid faeces. Flatulent colic.

sections.label: Rectum

Interior of anus studded with itching
eminence. Heemorrhoids. Liquid faeces.

sections.text:
Superficial ulcers and sores on lower ex-
tremities, especially in females at climacteric.

Vertigo, with inclination to fall forwards, 3 .—Vertigo, while
standing in the open air, 4 .—Giddiness and dizziness, with the sensation of
fulness over the eyes, 34 .—Duluess and headache, with sleepiness, in the

morning, 3 \—* Headache , alternating with diarrhoea , 3 .—Headache and fever
(third and fourth days), 20 .—Heavy dull pain in the forehead, with soreness
over the seat of pain, 3 .—Pain in the left frontal protuberance, aggravated
in the afternoon, 3 .—Momentary darts of pain in the forehead/obliging one
to shut the eyes, attended with giddiness, 3 .—[10.] Sudden pain in the fore¬
head, with soreness of the throat, in the evening, 3 .—After stool, at 10 a.m.,
frontal headache, with feverishness (first day), 17 .—Sensation of great (|ry-
ness of the forehead and eyes, which was relieved for a short time by bath¬
ing the parts with cold water ; after stool, at 10 A.M. (first day), 17 . — Press¬
ing pain in the temples, in the forenoon, with drawing in the eyes, as if
strabismus would follow, 3 .—Stunning headache through the temples, re¬
lieved by pressure, 3 .—Morning, headache, with heat in the vertex, 3 .—Pain
on the top of the head, when rising in the morning, 3 .

Eye .—The inflammation of the eyes is attended with a most excruci¬
ating heavy pain, and great turgescence of the vessels of the conjunctiva, 2 .
—Inflamed eyes, 18 .—Extensive superficial ulceration of each cornea, at¬
tended by genera] conjunctival congestion; the ulceration was central and
large in extent; in the right eye its base was densely white, and looked
exactly as if lead had been used (after ten days). No symptoms of irri¬
tation appeared while he was at work or during that evening, but on waking
next morning, his eyes were inflamed, 19 .—[20.] Left eye sore and uncom¬
fortable, especially at the inner canthus; conjunctiva of the left eyeball
slightly red, especially at the inner canthus, 16 .—Eyes glazed and motion¬
less (next morning), (in the elder), 7 .—Eyes sunken in their orbits, 7 .—
Heaviness of the eyes, with occasional pains on the top of the head, 3 .—
Drawing sensation in the eyes, accompanying pain in the head, 3 .—Smart¬
ing of the eyes, 3 .—Inflammation of the eyelids, 8 .—Pain in the eyeballs,
and in the temples, with heat, and throbbing of the temporal arteries, 3 .

sections.label: Nose
sections.text:
Soreness and little pustules in the nose, 8 .—Noses pinched, 7 .

^(^.—[30.] Faces pale as corpses, 7 .—The under jaw fallen (next
morning), (in the elder), 7 .

IHoutll. —The teeth are covered with dried mucus, in the morning, 3 .—

* Tongue white (fourth day), 20 .—White fur on the tongue, except the centre
(fifth day ), 20 .—* Tongue coated white, with much viscid mucus in the mouth
(first morning), 17 .—Sourness of the mouth, 3 .—Dryness of the mouth and
tongue, on waking in the morning, 3 .—Copious salivation, 3 .—Everything
tasted sweet (fifth day), 20 .—[40.] The taste of fried liver in the mouth, at
night, 3 .—Had a bad taste in the mouth for several days after the most
prominent symptoms had disappeared, 17 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Soreness in the left side of the throat, especially painful
when swallowing liquids, and worse in the morning, 3 .—* Soreness of the
throat, extending to the ears, 3 . —The elder complained frequently of burning
sensation in the throat , 7 .—* Dryness of the throat, 3 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Appetite and Thirst. Appetite much impaired, with
unusual thirst for cold water (first morning), 17 .—* Indifference to food 3 . —
*Loss of appetite. 3 ; (second day), 13 .—* Desire for something sour, 3 . —[50.]

* Great thirst,''; (fourth and fifth days), 20 .—Increased thirst after eating
(first day), 17 .—Thirst, towards evening, 3 .— Nausea and Vomiting.

to vomit, which lasted two hours (immediately), 111 .—Blight nausea accom¬
panied the diminution of pulse (three hours after three pills), 1 .— Acidity in

the afternoon, with an unpleasant sickly sensation in the stomach, 3 .—After
rising in the morning, had a sick feeling in the stomach, with occasional
nausea (first morning), 17 .—[60.] Vomiting had been going on for the last
four hours almost without intermission ; the vomited matters consisted, for
the most part, of seeds, pulp, and membranous covering of the ripe May
apple, having the peculiar odor of that fruit; afterwards the elder *vom-
ited bilious matter mixed with blood, the bile dark-green and very thick, the
blood dark and coagulated; she continued to vomit thick bile, with more or
less blood mixed with it, about every hour through the night ,\—* Vomited the
contents of the stomach, and then considerable bile (after nine hours); felt
better ; vomited again (after twelve hours), 20 .—* Vomiting of hot frothy
mucus, 3 . — Stomach. Epigastrium and entire abdomen tympanitic and
very tender (in the elder girl), 7 .—The stomach contracted so hard and
rapidly, in efforts to vomit, that the wrenching pain would cause them to
utter sharp screams, one after another, for five minutes at a time, 7 .—Ten¬
derness over the stomach (second day), (in the younger), 7 .—Great tender¬
ness over the stomach and bowels, scarcely bearing the pressure of the bed¬
clothes (fourth day), 20 .—Tender over stomach and bowels, increased by the
least motion ; could scarcely bear to be touched (fifth day), 20 .— *Sensation
of hollowness in the epigastrium, 3 .— *Had an empty feeling in the stomach,
before supper, but did not feel hungry (first day), 17 .—[70.] *Had a feeling
of weakness in the epigastric region, at 2 A.M., which continued until the
next morning (second night), 17 .—Awakened by violent pains in the stom¬
ach and bowels; the pains were of a griping, stitching character, and were
relieved for a short time by pressure on the bowels, at 3 a.m. (first night), 17 .
—Soon after eating some toast, pain commenced in the stomach, extending
into the bowels; increasing with such severity that she could not resist
screaming at every breath (fifth day), 20 .—In the night felt pain in the
stomach, which continued to increase in severity, and was attended with
much thirst and burning sensation, and great sense of prostration (first
night), 20 .—After breakfast, had a violent burning in the stomach, as if
caused by hot steam ; same sensation after dinner (first day), 17 .—Cold water
does not agree, it causes much oppression and uneasiness in the stomach ;
small quantities of it were ejected, which tasted very bitter, and caused
much burning in the oesophagus (first day), 17 .—Heat in the stomach, 3 .—
Throbbing in the epigastrium, followed by diarrhoea, 3 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Fulness in the right hypochondrium, with flatulence, 3 .—
Twisting pain in the right hypochondrium, with the sensation of heat in
the part, 3 .—[80.] Sensation of flatus in the left hypochondrium, 34 .—Sen¬
sation of weight and dragging in the left hypochondrium, close under the
ribs, 3 .—Stitches in the right hypochondrium, worse while eating, 3 .—Abdo¬
men swelled almost to bursting (next morning), (in the elder), 7 .—A good
deal of flatulence was caused, in the evening (first day), 12 .— * Flatulence
(second morning), I2b ; (second day), 13 .—Rumbling of flatus in the ascend¬
ing colon, 4 .— Violent colic, followed by liquid stools, which were repeated
until 9 o’clock (second day), lla .—Griping pains (second day), 13 .—Some
griping pains with the stools (second day), 12a .—[90.] Some wandering pains
in the abdomen, at 5 p.M., 1?a . —Pain in the bowels, at daylight in the morn¬
ing, which is relieved by external warmth, and by bending forward whilst
lying on the side, but is aggravated by lying ou the back, 3 .— *Pain in the
transverse colon, at 3 a.m., followed by diarrhoea 3 .—* Severe pain in the bowels
(after five hours), 20 .—Pain in the bowels occasionally, but not so severe
(fourth day), 20 .—Pain in the ascending colon, 4 .—* Sensation of heat in the


133

bowels, accompanying the inclination to go to stool, 3 . —After supper, sensation
as it there would be an evacuation of the bowels. This sensation came
and went at short intervals, until going to bed, when it ceased (first day), 17 .
—Awoke at 2 a.m., with slight stitching pains in bowels, with desire to go
to stool ; did not sleep well the remaining part of the night, on account of
occasional stitching pains in the bowels; the pains were mitigated by flexing
the thighs on the abdomen (second night), 17 .—The symptoms generally,
but especially the abdominal symptoms, are aggravated in the morning
and better in the evening, 3 .— [100] Teuderness and some bloating of lower
bowels (fifth day) ; still very tender over lower bowels (sixth day), 20 .—Pain
had extended into the lower bowels and right ovary, in the afternoon (fifth
day), .

Hectam a nil Anus. — * Aggravation of internal piles; the rectum
would protrude more than an inch after every motion of the bowels or after
any sudden motion, such as sneezing, and even during any mental excitement;
the parts could not always be replaced very readily; would sometimes remain
prolapsed for days, owing to the swelling a,nd congestion , u .—Too much bear¬
ing down at stool, as if from inactivity of the rectum, 3 .—Secretion of mucus
from the anus, 3 .

early in the morning, which continues through the forenoon, followed by

—Increased action of the bowels (after nine and five hours); purgation

mucus, and was of an offensive odor; about 10 a.m., had another evacua¬
tion, which was accompanied with violent tenesmus, lasting some time after the

ing two more thin dejections resulted, attended with some griping pains,
and an uncomfortable feeling of chilliness, 12a .—Bowels moved twice, but
not copiously, attended with very much pain and deadly nausea (after
twelve hours), 20 .—No movement of the bowels since the second day, but
felt like it several times (fourth day), 20 .— [120.] *Diarrhcea and constipa¬
tion, alternating every day or two, for several days after the most prominent
symptoms had. disappeared , u .

POLYGONUM.

Polygonum acre, H. B. K. (P. punctatum, Ell.; P. hydropiperoides,
Pursh). The closely allied species, P. hydropiper, L., is not perennial, but
in other respects is very similar to P. acre; both possess properties nearly,
if not absolutely, identical. These are the only American acrid species.

Natural order, Polygonacese.

Common names, Smart Weed, Water Pepper, etc.

Preparation, Tincture of the whole plant.

tinued through the day, but mostly when within doors, scarcely felt when
in open air (sixth day), 1 .—Pulsative and erratic pains continue, especially
when in the house (seventh day), 1 .—Erratic pains continue (eighth and
ninth days), 1 .

sections.text:
Skin of the whole body dry (after second dose, fifteenth day), 2 .
—In the evening a scarlet eruption, about three inches in width, made its
appearance around the waist, itching and burning, attended with pain

ling in the whole body, more in legs and feet, forearm and hands (nine¬
teenth day), 2 .

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
[ 210 .] Restless sleep, with unpleasant dreams; awoke unre¬
freshed (ninth day), 2 .—Uneasy sleep aud dreams (fourteenth day), 2 .—
Dreams, but could not recall them (tenth day), 2 .—Dreamed of having a se¬
vere headache, and awoke with the head aching violently (after third dose,
fifteenth day), 2 .—Laborious and fatiguing dreams (sixteenth day), 2 .

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Alternations of chills and heat (after second dose, fifteenth
day), 2 .—Feet alternately cold and hot (thirteenth day), 2 .—Great heat and
burning of the feet, continuing one and a half hours, and then suddenly
becoming uncomfortably cold (third day), 2 .—Profuse perspiration and
trembling of the whole body, from moderate exercise (third day), 2 .

tion in neck of bladder; cutting in neck of bladder.—( After walking),

sections.label: Mind
sections.text:
* Mind gloomy and desponding (second day), 56 .— * Gloomy and
desponding, and even morose (ninth day), 6 .—* Very sad and gloomy ,'*.—Low-
spirited and irritable (sixth day), 26 .—Very dull and depressed all day, 2d .—
Feel dull and indisposed to exertion (seventh day); for five days succeed¬
ing this I had not my usual appetite or spirits ; suffered from a general
feeling of not being quite well, but without any special describable pains
or symptoms ; it was precisely the feeling of one who is said to be bilious, 21 ’.

sections.label: Head
sections.text:
My head is feeling very light and hollow, with deep frontal
headache, in the morning (sixth day), 1 .—Head feeling light (seventh day), 1 .
— *Light dizzy feeling in the head (third day), 6 . —[ 10 .] Slight feeling of ful¬
ness in the head (sixth day)/ b .—Awoke with a dull pain in the head, which
continued all day; thought it might be due to a glass of ale drank the
evening before (third day); awoke with a dull pain in the head, with sen¬
sation of soreness in the brain, increased by stooping or shaking the head ;
this headache is precisely similar to that experienced on the third, which 1
attributed to the glass of ale ; I now believe that the pain at that time was
caused by the Polyporus (seventh day), 2b .— *Dull headache (third day), 4 *.
—Dull feeling in head (tenth day), 3 .— *Dull aching pain in the head (after
ten hours, sixth day), 6 .—Severe headache, aggravated by motion (after
seven hours, third day), 6 .—Pain in the head, jaws, and teeth (fifth day), 6 .
—Head ached severely all night (third night), 1 .—* Headache, qualmishness,
relieved by eructations (third day), 4 *.—Most of the head symptoms greatly
aggravated (after four hours, fourth day), 5 . —[ 20 .] Severe semilateral
headache (ninth day), 5 .— Forehead. *Dull frontal headache, lasting all
day (after half an hour), 1 .—Continued dulness of the forehead, with slight
aching (first day), 4 *.—Dull frontal headache (third day), 1 ; (tenth day), 3 .
—Dull frontal headache (fourth day) ; in the evening (fifth day), 3 .—Dul¬
ness of the forehead (second day), 1 .—Dull, heavy pain in the forehead,
worse on motion (second night), 6 .—Heaviness of the forehead (fourth
day), 4 *.—At 8 a.m., violent frontal headache ; very much aggravated by
walking; head feels light and hollow (fourth day), 1 .—Hard frontal head¬
ache (fifth day), 1 .— [ 30 .] Violent frontal headache, with an extremely
light, hollow feeling of the head ; the headache is greatly aggravated by
walking (sixth day), 1 .—Deep frontal headache for the last forty-eight
hours (seventh day), 6 .—Frontal headache, aggravated by motion (second
day), 6 .—Continuous oppressive headache in forehead and temples, all day
(sixth day), 3 .—In the evening tight feeling in the forehead, with slight

headache (second day) ; tightness of the forehead as yesterday (third day), 4 .
—Tightness across the forehead, with dull headache (fifth day), 4 .—Mo
mentary twinge over the left eyebrow (sixth day), 26 .— Temples. Dull
pains through temples (second day), 3 .—Dull, heavy pains through temples
and in forehead (ninth day), 3 .—Aching soreness through temples (seventh
day), 3 .— [ 40 .] Lacerating pain in the right temple, at 9.40 p.M., ?c .—Neu¬
ralgic pain in the temples (second day), 5 .—Neuralgic pains in the temples,

Frequent cutting pain in the temples (after ten hours), 6 .—Severe pain in

Eye .— [ 50 .] Eyeballs ache severely (sixth day), 1 .—Deep drawing pain

sections.label: Face
sections.text:
Face of a bluish color (fourth day), 5 .—Pain in the jaws, teeth,
and head (fifth day), 6 .

sections.label: Mouth
sections.text:
Teeth and Gums. Teeth feel as if they were being
forced out of their sockets (fourth day), 5 .—Teeth and gums became very
sore, 1 *.—Gums and teeth are all sore (seventh day), 1 .—Gums sore (fourth
day), 5 .— Tongue. * Tongue coated white (third day), 6 .—* Yellow tinge of
tongue (ninth day), 3 .— [ 60 .] * Yellow coating of tongue (tenth day), 3 ; (eighth
day), 6 .— * Tongue is coated thickly, yellow (sixth and seventh days), 1 .—
Tongue coated light brown (fourth day), 6 .—Tongue red at the tip,and coated
yellow at the base (fifth day), 1 .—Prick ling in the end of the tongue, which soon
passed away (after one hour), 2 *.— Taste. *Bitter taste in the mouth (sixth
day), 1 ; (eighth day), 6 .—Bitter, coppery taste in the mouth (seventh day), 1 .
—Flat, metallic, or coppery taste (ninth day), 3 .—Constant coppery taste in
the mouth, 1 *.—Slight coppery taste in the mouth and throat (after four hours,

seous taste (tenth day), 3 .

sections.label: Throat
sections.text:
Rawness and scraping in the throat, all the afternoon and
evening (sixth day), 25 .—Feeling in the fauces as if I would vomit, but no
nausea (third day), 1 .

sections.label: Stomach
sections.text:
Appetite and Thirst. Appetite invigorated (fourth
day), 3 .—Very little appetite (ninth day); little appetite (tenth day), 3 .—
Not so much appetite for breakfast as common (fourth day), 2 .—No appe¬
tite for supper, which is contrary to my usual habit (sixth day), 26 .—At 1
p.M., poor appetite for dinner (eleventh day) ; slight diminution of appe¬
tite for forty-eight hours, 2c , —[ 80 .] *Loss of appetite, la .—Desire for sour
things, which have always relieved the symptoms (tenth day), 3 .— *Much
thirst (third day), 4 *.— Eructations and Heartburn . Eructations
(third day), 4 *.—Heartburn, with acid risings (sixth day), 25 .— Nausea
and Vomiting. *Nausea (after twenty minutes, sixth day), 2b .—Fre¬
quent spells of nausea, lasting but a momeut (third day), 1 .—Nausea at the
stomach (after four hours), 5 .—Nausea and slight vomiting of a sour watery
fluid, intensely bitter (after four hours, fourth day), 5 .—Some nausea, par¬
ticularly in throat (second day) ; nausea at times (third day) ; particularly
in throat and fauces (sixth day), 8 .— [ 90 .] Felt sick at stomach (ninth
day), 3 .—Qualmishness, with the loose stool (second day); qualmishness,
headache, relieved by eructations (third day), 4 *.— Stomach. Tonic effects,

invigorated digestion (third, fourth, and fifth days), 3 .—Effects decidedly
tonic (fifth day); instead of being tonic as befpre, its effects were now
enervating (ninth day), 3 .—Deep distress in the epigastrium, lasting all day,
with dull pains in the right hypochondrium, and sharp pains in the epi¬
gastrium ; aggravated by walking (after half an hour), 1 .—Dull, aching,

night), 1 .—Great burning distress in the region of the stomach and liver,

stool; continues after a stool (fourth day), 1 .—The most terrible distress be¬
tween the stomach and navel, lasted all the afternoon ; could not get relief
in any position ; accompanied by great faintness and high fever (fifth day), 1 .
—Burning pain in the stomach, with dragging pain in the hypochondrium
(first and second days), 6 .— [ 100 .] Burning in the epigastrium (after four
hours, sixth day), 6 .—In evening, feeling as if lump in stomach (sixth day), 3 .
—Coldness of stomach, followed by burning (after several hours, seventh
day), 3 .—Dull aching pain in the stomach and bowels (ninth day), 5 .—Pain
in the epigastrium (after four hours), 5 .—Pain in stomach (after four hours,
and eighth day), 5 ; (fourth day), 6 .—Pain in the stomach and liver (third
day), 5 .—Pain in the stomach and bowels, almost unbearable (after four
hours, fourth day), 5 .—Woke at midnight with hard, cutting pains in the
epigastrium (second night) ; at 5 A.M., awoke with the same cutting pains
in the epigastric region, and distress in the umbilicus, with great desire for
stool (third morning), 1 . — Severe sharp cutting pains in stomach and
bowels (sixth day), 3 .—[HO.] During the day very sharp pains in the stom¬
ach, almost constant borborygmus (seventh day), 3 .—Sharp, cutting, lanci¬
nating pains in the stomach (ninth day), 3 .

sections.label: Abdomen
sections.text:
Hypochondria. Dull, heavy, aching pains in the
region of the right lobe of the liver, after the morning stool (third day), 1 .

— Dull, heavy, drawing pains in the region of the right lobe of the liver,
extending through to the dorsal region (third day), 1 .—Heavy dragging
pains in the right lobe of the liver (third night), 1 . — 1 p.m., have had con¬
stant and severe aching distress in the right lobe of the liver, lower part
of the epigastrium and upper part of the umbilicus (fifth day), 1 .—Distress
in the right hypochondrium and umbilicus (fifth day), 1 .—A full inspiration
produces sharp, stabbing pains in the right lobe of the liver and lower
dorsal region (fifth day), 1 .—Great distress in the region of the liver and
small intestines, with the stool, at 9 a.m. (sixth day), 1 . — Dull aching dis¬
tress in the right lobe of liver and umbilicus, with great desire for stool
(sixth day), 1 .— [ 120 .] Dull dragging pains in the region of the right lobe
of the liver (seventh day), 1 .—Pain in the liver and stomach (third day), 5 .
—Dragging pain in the hypochondrium, with burning pain in the stomach
(first and second days), 6 .—Dragging in the right hypochondrium (after
four hours, sixth day), 6 .—Dull aching pain in the liver (after ten hours,
sixth day), 6 .—Dragging pain in the liver (sixth day), 6 .—Severe pain in
the liver (sixth day), 5 .—Pain in the liver (eighth day), 5 .—Hard pain in
the region of the spleen and left epigastric region (after three hours, fourth
day), 6 .—Sharp pain in the spleen, liver, and bowels (third and fifth days), 6 .

— [ 130 .] Sharp pain in the region of the spleen (after four hours, sixth
day), 6 .—Frequent sharp pains in the spleen (after ten hours, sixth day), 6 .

— Umbilicus. Severe distress in the umbilical and hypogastric region,
with great desire for stool (third day), 1 .—Slight uneasiness in subumbilical

region, which gradually increased, with inclination to go to stool, having
about an hour previously had my usual morning stool ; during the stool
which followed, a shooting pain extended upon each side of the umbilicus,

what, but did not entirely disappear after stool (third day), 2 .—Distress in

—Sharp pain in the umbilical and hypogastric regions (after ten hours,
sixth day), 6 . —General Abdomen. Rumbling in the bowels (third
day), 5 .—Loud borborygmus (first day), 1 .—Dull aching distress in the whole
abdomen, with loud "borborygmus (third day), 1 .—Great rumbling in the

day), 3 .—Emission of fetid flatulence, in the evening (fifth day), 3 .—Much

bowels (fourth day), 6 .—Pain in the region of the transverse colon, and in

throughout the abdomen, for about five minutes ; the pains then became
located in the hypogastric region, and continued one hour, with slight in¬
clination to go to stool ; the pains then became easier, though they had
not entirely passed away at tea-time ; felt again ten minutes after a stool,
in the lower portion of the abdomen, extending to the right hypochondrium,
at 9.40 p.m., 2c . —Uneasiness of the bowels (first day), 4 *. — [ 160 .] Slight
aching uneasiness in the whole abdomen, with slight pain all night (second
day), 4 *.—Continued pain over the whole abdomen (third day), 4 *.—Uneasi¬
ness in the abdomen, during the night (fourth day), 4a .—Some uneasiness
in bowels, from increased vermicular action (fourth and fifth days), 3 .—
Slight uneasiness, as if I would have a stool ; this soon passed away (after
one hour), 2a .—Slight uneasiness in the bowels after retiring (fourth night), 2 .
—Twice during the day had slight pain in the bowels (general), (third
day), 4 .—Sensation as if diarrhoea would come on (fifth day), 4 .—Uneasiness
of the abdomen, with looseness of the bowels (sixth day), 4 .—Very sudden
and severe distress in the hypogastric region, followed by papescent stools,
stools very light-colored (after four hours, sixth day), 6 .— [ 170 .] Soon after
the chilliness felt a slight momentary pain in hypogastric region; in a few
minutes experienced similar pains in both hypochondria (sixth day), 2b .—
This morning have a dull aching pain over the whole lower abdomen
(fourth day), 4 .—Uneasiness in the lower abdomen all day, as if diarrhoea
would come on (fourth day), 4 .

Rectum and Anus. —Pain in the anus (third day), 5 .—Severe pain
in the anus (third day), 6 .—Unpleasant sensation, not amounting to pain,
about the anus; not felt after 1 p.m. (third day), 2 .—Desire for stool, with.

A.M., soon passed off (fifth day), 2 .—A disposition to go to stool, with some
pain in the anus (after four hours), 5 .—Disposition to go to stool (third

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
* Loose stool, at 6 a.m. ; soft mushy stool, mixed with mucus, at
6 p.m., the medicine having acted as a mild cathartic in eight hours (second
day) ; soft, mushy stool, at 5 A.M., followed by dull, heavy, aching pains in
the region of the right lobe of the liver; after 8 p.m., stool of a dark color,
mixed with bile and mucus, followed by a dull aching distress in the dor¬
sal region, extending up to the shoulders, on both sides (third day); at 6
a.m., very black-colored stool, mixed with bile and mucus ; before the stool
I voided about 1 drachm of white mucus ; after 8 a.m., stool that ran a
stream from the bowels, of bile, mucus, and black fecal matter, followed
by burning distress in region of stomach and liver, extending down to the
umbilicus ; at 10 a.m., copious stool of water and black fecal matter, with
great desire to strain after stool, followed by same symptoms as before ; it
will be seen by this experiment that 40 grains of the Polyporus, well trit¬
urated, will act as a violent hydragogue cathartic in two hours, if it is
taken on an empty stomach (fourth day) ; in the morning, hard, black,
lumpy stool, mixed with bile and mucus ; at 1 p.m., soft, black, fetid,
papescent stool, followed by the most terrible distress between the stomach
and navel (fifth day); in the morning, dark papescent stool ; mushy stool
at 9 a.m., with great distress in the region of the liver and small intestines;
at 6 p.m., papescent stool, followed by about one teaspoonful of blood, with
severe tenesmus (sixth day) ; soft, mushy stool (seventh day) ; papescent,
dark colored stool, without pain (eighth day) ; my bowels have been loose
every day, with from one to three stools a day, without pain ; all have been
of a dark color; to-day my stool is natural, and I am feeling well (thir¬
teenth day), 1 .-—Loose stool, with qualmishness (second day) ; at 9 a.m., at

3.30 p.m., copious fluid stool, expelled with great force, and another of the
same character at 4 (third day); a loose, yellow stool, with pain after¬
wards, at 9 a.m. ; loose stool, with pain, at 6 p.m. (fourth day) ; bowels
loose (fifth day); loose stool, with tenesmus, at 2 and 3 p.m. (sixth day) ;
six days have elapsed since the last dose, and my bowels have not become
regular yet (ninth day), 41 .—Copious, soft, mushy stool, followed by slight
uneasiness in the umbilical region, at 3.30 p.m. (sixth day) ; scanty stool,
at 9 a.m. (seventh day), 2b .—Soft, mushy stool, unattended with pain, at

9.30 p.m., 2 ®. —Soft mushy stool, at 9 p.m., similar to the one in the morning,
but without the accompanying symptoms (third day); no stool at the usual
time, but a mushy one at 9.30 a.m., preceded by the same pains in the
lower portion of the abdomen, which immediately passed off after stool
(fourth day); usual stool after breakfast (fifth day), 2 . — Slight motion
of the bowels (fifth day), 4 .—Two stools, in the morning (fourth day), 6 .—
Stools the first part of the day dry and lumpy, but in the evening were
quite frequent, thin, watery, and very yellow (fifth day), 6 .—Very light-
colored, papescent stools, followed distress in hypogastric region (after four
hours, sixth day), 6 .—[190.] Soft papescent stools during the last forty-
eight hours (seventh day), 6 .—Copious and watery stools, accompanied with
severe pains (fourth day), 5 .—Stools dark, dry, and lumpy, followed with
stools mixed with bile and mucus; stools mixed with blood ; stools thin
and yellow (fifth day), 5 .—One copious stool, at 3 p.m. (ninth day), 5 .—The
stools were not so black, and all contained more or less undigested food,
and were mixed with water; also a number contained something that had

147

the appearance of oil ; it was in drops, from the size of a common new
cent down to small drops ; the color was clear and white ; was it oil or
not?, 1 ®.—Passage of dry, hard feces (tenth day), 3 .— * Bowels costive (ninth
day), 3 ; (eighth day), 6 .

Urinary Organs. —Increased urination (ninth day), 3 .— Frequent
passage of high-colored urine, with pain in the region of the kidneys (third
day), 3 .—*Urine diminished and high-colored (sixth day), 5 .— [ 200 .] * Urine
very high-colored and scanty (fifth day), 1 .—Increased secretion of urine
(sixth day), 3 .—Increased desire to urinate (seventh day), 3 .—Frequent de¬
sire to urinate (tenth day), 3 .—Frequent urination during the night (first
night), 4 .—Urine acid and profuse, light-colored (fifth day), 4 .—Passed urine
freely, at 10 A.M., 12 m., 2, 4, 6, and 9 p.m. ; pale, almost colorless; desire
to pass urine was constant (second day) ; constant desire to urinate; passed
urine profusely, at 10 a.m., 12 M., and 2 p.m. (third day) ; profuse urination
(fourth day), 4 ®.

Sexual Organs .—Soon after getting into bed, at 10 p.m., a sharp
pain in the glatis penis, very severe, 2 '.

sections.label: Chest
sections.text:
Pain in the left lung (third day), 6 .—Sharp darting pains iu
the left lung, with slight suffocating feeling, causing me to rise up in bed,
lasting four hours (fourth day), 5 .— [ 210 .] Dull aching in the left lung, ex¬
tending through the left shoulder-blade (ninth day), 5 .—Pain in the ribs,
aggravated by motion (after six hours), 6 .

Heart and Pulse .—Sharp piercing pain in the region of the heart,
aggravated by motion (after six hours), 6 .—*Pulse 110, full and soft (fifth
day), 1 .—Pulse 100, at 6 p.m. ; 90 at 9 p.m. (sixth day), 1 .—Pulse from 90
to 105 (first night), 5 .—Pulse 90, full and wiry (ninth day), 5 .—Pulse 100,
full and soft (seventh day), 6 .

Neck and Back. — Neck. Slight drawing pains in the left side of
the neck, after getting into bed, at 10 p.m., 2 ®.— A slight pain shot up the
back of the neck, from between the shoulder-blades, followed by a little
soreness of the occipital region, with disposition to throw the head back ;
this soon disappeared (third day), 2 . — Back. [ 220 .] * Severe backache
(fourth day), 1 .—Severe backache; back is very stiff; can hardly rise up
after sitting down a few minutes (seventh day), 1 .— *Dull aching pain in the
back and hips (third day), 6 .—Dull pain in the back (after four hours, sixth
day), 6 .—Dull aching pain iu the back (after ten hours, sixth day), 6 .—5
p.m., back very painful and stiff (seventh day), 6 .—Dull and aching pain in
the back and limbs (second day), 5 .—Drawing pains, several times through
the day, in the back and legs (first day), 4 . — jDorsal. Rheumatic pains
in the spine and limbs, lasting four hours (fourth day), 5 .—Dull aching
distress in the dorsal region, extending up to the shoulders, on both sides,
after a stool (third day), 1 .— [ 230 .] Great aching distress in the dorsal and
lumbar region (sixth day), 1 .— Lumbar. Hard aching distress in the
lumbar region (third night), 1 .—Dull aching distress in the lumbar region
(sixth day), 1 .—Dull pains in the lumbar region (third day), 1 .—Pain and
weakness in the small of the back (sixth day), 5 .—Dull pain in the small
